attack_mechanism: Reading or probing `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r6` after the transfer provides an alternate observation point even if R4 itself is protected. This mechanism uses the chain `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r4 -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_src -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.reg_incr_val -> openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r6`. `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r6` stores or forwards that copied value after the destination write edge; the relevant assignment conditions include `openMSP430.execution_unit_0.register_file_0.r6_wr`. A register-to-register instruction can select R4 on `reg_src` and write the unchanged or ALU-transformed result into another architectural register. The attacker obtains the R4 word, or a reversible transform of it, through a less protected register location.
